text:
Maya: quick sync - we need a final take on chat input shape for next sprint planning
Jules: customers ask for both a simple `prompt` and a message array for multi-turn state
Sam: runtime note: messages array enables role-aware KV reuse and cheaper delta caches; single `prompt` is easiest for legacy sync path
Priya: design: messages maps cleanly to UI threads (avatars, role labels). `prompt` becomes concat + heuristics which UX hates
Tom: support: two asks - (1) smooth migration from `prompt`, (2) enforcement around system role so system instructions aren’t dropped by accident
Maya: proposal: make `messages` canonical. Accept `prompt` as a legacy alias server-side (canonicalize to messages) to avoid SDK churn
Jules: server-side canonicalization is critical for consistent token counting and billing attribution (+1)
Sam: canonicalization rules must be deterministic. example: `prompt` -> `[{role: \"system\", content: DEFAULT_SYSTEM}, {role: \"user\", content: prompt}]`
Priya: edge: what if request sends both `messages` and `prompt`? We should avoid silent merges
Maya: candidate: default behavior = 400 error if both present. allow override with `merge_mode: \"append_prompt_to_messages\"` or `merge_mode: \"prepend\"`
Tom: make the 400 error actionable: include migration link + code snippets. That reduces support load
Sam: function/tool calling: message-level metadata helps (e.g., `metadata: {call_tool: true}`) so router/runtime can annotate traces and enforce policies
Jules: roles - do we permit arbitrary role strings? customers request custom roles for skill attribution and cross-service calls
Maya: we keep normative roles `system|user|assistant`. support optional `role_type` (canonical|custom). custom roles allowed for enterprise with a whitelist toggle
Priya: structured output: if assistant emits structured JSON, we should pair with `response_type: structured` in the response envelope and surface schema in console
Sam: runtime constraints: messages array helps avoid re-tokenizing assistant outputs. single prompt will force full re-tokenization and break KV reuse, increasing cost
Jules: telemetry/billing: messages gives per-role token provenance which we need for per-route cost breakdowns and per-user chargeback
Tom: rollout plan sketch: 1) server canonicalization + helpful errors; 2) SDK sugar wrappers; 3) migrate top legacy customers w/ support emails; 4) deprecate raw `prompt` in 12 months
Maya: launch criteria checklist candidate:
- messages canonical input + `prompt` alias handled server-side
- deterministic canonicalization documented
- merge_mode options documented + default reject with actionable error
- system role enforcement with enterprise opt-out `allow_system_omit`
- message-level metadata hooks for tool-calling and embeddings
- SDK updates (js, py, go) with client helpers
- perf safety: p99 latency impact <10% on representative workloads
- console telemetry: token provenance + role breakdowns
Priya: prioritization: MVP = canonicalization + docs + SDK helpers. Next = metadata-driven tool hooks + merge modes. Later = enterprise role whitelists + fine-grained admin controls
Jules: I'll raise RFC with eng + legal for role handling and data classification implications
Sam: adding to RFC: KV invalidation rules, token counting for canonicalization, fallback if messages exceed token window
Tom: I'll draft the customer comms and include migration snippets (curl + node + py) and a 12-month deprecation timeline
Maya: ok locking this as the decision note to bring into sprint planning, please add any blockers by EOD

Maya: example error we should return for conflicting input:
```
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
{
  "error": "Conflicting input: both `messages` and `prompt` provided. Set `merge_mode` to override or send only `messages`. See https://redwood.dev/migration/chat-input for migration steps."
}
```

Jules: thumbs ✅ on the error text. also include a code example for canonicalization behavior in docs
Sam: runtime will provide a test harness and perf numbers for the RFC
Priya: I'll add UI samples showing how to render messages and how to map legacy prompts
Tom: support will collect top 10 customers on `prompt` usage and reach out with migration help
Maya: great. moving this into RFC draft and pinging eng/release owners
